To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bootstrap confidence intervals are the most effective tool for interpreting SCs when sample size is greater than 100.

(a) the bootstrap confidence interval method provides the most accurate estimates of structure coefficient confidence intervals, (b) the bootstrap confidence intervals are more accurate for larger sample sizes, (c) the rules of thumb provide the most accurate estimates for smaller sample sizes, and (d) nonnormality and unequal covariance matrices diminish the accuracy of all confidence interval estimates.

(1) the use of confidence intervals is recommended for the interpretation of structure coefficients in discriminant analysis when sample sizes exceed 100; (2) the use of rules of thumb is recommended for the use of confidence interval for the interpretation of discriminant analysis structure coefficients in samples of fewer than 100; (3) the use of structure coefficients is less useful for the interpretation of the discriminant function when the data are nonnormal or the covariance matrices are unequal.
